subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should repeated calls with identical arguments and the same structured nonzero exec outcome count as no progress even when their output text changes meaningfully?
rationale: Source, tests, and live proof establish that the implementation works, but only an owner can choose the intended balance between stopping runaway retries and permitting legitimate nonzero polling workflows with evolving output.

options.title: Accept stable nonzero fingerprints
options.body: Approve the current policy because identical arguments and structured nonzero outcomes are sufficient evidence of no progress once the configured threshold is reached.

options.title: Preserve meaningful nonzero output
options.body: Require a narrower normalization or additional progress discriminator before merge so changing nonzero output can keep a retry sequence alive when it reflects real state changes.

options.title: Pause the heuristic change
options.body: Keep the existing behavior until a more explicit exec progress contract can distinguish volatile failure noise from meaningful nonzero progress.

recommendation.title: Accept stable nonzero fingerprints
recommendation.body: Approve the current policy because identical arguments and structured nonzero outcomes are sufficient evidence of no progress once the configured threshold is reached.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed the real foreground contract and have recent relevant history across exec and loop-detection behavior.
